source_snapshot.procedure: Send DCMI raw 0x2c/0x04 with DCh group ID, action, two-byte watt limit described as MS-byte first, four-byte correction time, two reserved bytes and two-byte sampling period; then read with a misspelled `dcmitool` raw 0x2c/0x03.
source_snapshot.criteria: Set and Get complete without error and Get Power Limit matches the setting.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek correctly requires an operator-supplied watt limit and read-back but its high-level example sets only the watt field, omitting the source's exception action, correction time and sampling period, and does not establish whether the limit is activated.

original_test_intent.purpose: Write one approved static DCMI platform power-limit parameter set over OOB IPMI and verify the exact stored values with Get Power Limit; enforcement under workload is not demonstrated unless activation and a separate controlled limit-exceedance phase are explicitly added.
original_test_intent.target: The exact DCMI-capable SUT/BMC platform power-limit policy reached through protected `lanplus`, not a CPU-only, GPU-only, PSU or vendor Node Manager domain policy.
original_test_intent.scope: Capture current active/inactive limit, set one approved exception action, watt limit, correction time and statistics sampling period, read back all fields and restore the original policy under approval. Action 01h may hard-power-off the platform if an active limit is exceeded; 11h logs only. This row does not itself define Activate/Deactivate or a workload stimulus.
original_test_intent.operation: Verify DCMI version/capability and current power reading/limit, encode all multi-byte numeric fields least-significant byte first under IPMI convention, submit one complete raw Set request, validate response group ID/completion, issue standard Get, distinguish active versus no-active-limit status, compare every byte/decoded field, then restore and verify the baseline when required.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes and authorizes one set/get cycle. It does not authorize repeated dynamic limit changes or a load-duration enforcement test.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The BMC accepts only in-range values, echoes DCh and Get reports the exact action, watts, correction time and sampling period with reserved fields valid. Stored configuration and active state are reported separately. No hard power-off, workload throttling or SEL event should be claimed unless the owner separately activates and stimulates the limit.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: DCMI/BMC/SUT identity and capability; current power reading, active state and complete baseline; exact approved action/watts/correction/sampling values; little-endian encoded request; completion/response group ID; full Get response and field-by-field match; activation status; workload/power/SEL/OOB health; restoration and final read-back.
ambiguities: The source says watt bytes are MS-byte first, but DCMI follows IPMI's least-significant-byte-first convention unless otherwise specified; Table 6-18 supplies no MS-first exception.
The source omits Activate/Deactivate Power Limit even though DCMI recommends explicit activation after Set, so it cannot prove enforcement or exception action behavior.
The source does not supply exact values, platform achievable range, current power headroom or whether active state should change.
The merged high-level command sets only watts and therefore does not preserve the raw source's action/timing fields.
source_conflicts: The source's MS-byte-first instruction conflicts with the normative IPMI/DCMI byte-order convention and can encode the wrong power/timing values.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly keeps a high-risk approved mutation, requires exact fields, baseline, workload quiescence, fallback, read-back, restore and preserved SEL evidence. It repeats the source's incorrect MSB-first watt encoding, omits the standard explicit activation distinction, and expands the purpose to assessing action/timing behavior even though no Activate command or limit-exceedance stimulus exists.

applicable_history.decision: Historical confirmation requirements remain valid. No locked decision establishes MS-first encoding, exact limit fields or permission to activate and exceed the limit.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the capability class but rewrite the byte-level contract before execution. All multi-byte fields must follow IPMI little-endian order unless platform evidence says otherwise, and Set/Get configuration verification must be separated from activation/enforcement. The current source/V2 byte order could apply a drastically different power limit.

available_now: DCMI 1.5 defines complete Set/Get/Activate command layouts, actions, ranges-by-completion-code and static persistent policy intent.
Read-only DCMI capability, power reading, current limit/active state, SEL and system baseline can be collected before approval.
A qualified encoder can validate exact little-endian raw bytes offline without contacting the BMC.
missing_inputs: Exact approved action, watt limit, correction time, sampling period, desired active state and whether this case is configuration-only or includes a separately specified enforcement phase
Platform-supported/achievable ranges, normal and worst-case power envelope, workload quiescence or controlled stimulus, and expected action/SEL behavior
Qualified little-endian DCMI encoder/decoder and protected OOB route; confirmation whether the platform has any documented nonstandard byte-order behavior
Dedicated SUT, maintenance approval, alternate console, hard-power-off/data-integrity plan, baseline restore and recovery authority
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The platform/power owner supplies safe ranges and intent; the workload/lab owner supplies window and approval; the BMC/tool owner qualifies DCMI encoding and route; the recovery owner handles any exception action.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Query DCMI capability, current power reading, Get Power Limit, activation state, BMC health and preserved SEL without changing policy.
Offline encode/decode exact proposed values in little-endian form and review high-level tool behavior against raw bytes.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not send the source's MS-first payload, default any field, set watts alone when the test requires all fields, activate/deactivate, run a workload, clear SEL, select action 01h or restore blindly without exact approval.
Do not claim read-back proves power enforcement, throttling, hard-off timing or SEL correlation.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Owners sign exact values, byte order, static configuration versus enforcement scope, active-state plan, ranges and recovery; encoder produces reviewed raw bytes; baseline/fallback are proven; any activation/load phase is separated with its own duration, stop conditions and approval.

revision_candidate.test_name: OOB DCMI Static Power-Limit Configuration and Read-Back
revision_candidate.purpose: Set one approved static DCMI platform power-limit configuration over protected OOB IPMI, verify every stored field and active-state status, and restore the approved baseline without claiming enforcement behavior that was not stimulated.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact DCMI-capable BMC/SUT with documented achievable power limits, protected `lanplus`, dedicated maintenance window, quiesced workload or separately approved stimulus, independent console and recovery.
revision_candidate.target_scope: DCMI platform power-limit action, watts, correction time and statistics period only. Node Manager domain policies, GPU/CPU-specific caps and active enforcement testing are excluded unless separately defined.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: DCMI version/capabilities; exact safe values and desired activation state; platform range/power envelope; complete baseline; qualified little-endian encoder/decoder; protected credentials; maintenance/hard-off approval; workload, fallback, restore and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Preserve SEL and read capability/current power/current limit and active state. After fresh approval, encode DCh, reserved zeros, action, watts, correction time, reserved zeros and sampling period using IPMI least-significant-byte-first numeric order and send Set 04h once. Validate completion/DCh, run Get 03h, compare every field and report active state. Do not activate or exceed the limit unless a separate approved phase says so. Restore and verify the baseline as required.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC/SUT and DCMI support verified; exact values/ranges/byte order reviewed; dedicated window and data-safe workload state; protected OOB and fallback console; baseline/SEL captured; action 01h consequences explicitly approved; restore/recovery ready.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Capability/target/tool identity; current power/limit/active state; signed exact fields; reviewed raw little-endian bytes; redacted Set/Get responses, completions and DCh; field-by-field match; explicit enforcement-not-tested status; workload/power/SEL/OOB health; restore/final read-back.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel DCMI Specification v1.5 rev. 1.0 sections 6.6.2-6.6.4/Tables 6-17 to 6-19, IPMI 2.0 byte-order convention, and exact platform power-policy limits.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never use MS-first numeric encoding without documented exception, default fields, dynamically sweep limits, activate/stress implicitly, select hard-off without approval, clear SEL, expose credentials, auto-retry or leave an unapproved persistent policy.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Fresh platform/lab/workload owner approval is required for every field, desired active state, hard-off/log action, maintenance window and restoration before Set; activation/enforcement needs separate explicit approval.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners choose safe policy and whether enforcement is a separate test. The agent can perform one approved set/get/restore cycle and evidence collection; hard-off/data-impact judgment and exceptional recovery remain human-controlled.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On command/read-back mismatch, unexpected activation, power/workload impact or OOB instability, stop without retry, preserve SEL/power/session evidence, use independent console to stabilize the SUT and restore the recorded policy only with owner authorization, then verify active state and health.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Target/DCMI mismatch; unresolved byte order; missing exact values/ranges/approval/baseline/fallback; workload unsafe; action 01h unapproved; completion 84h/85h/89h or unexpected OEM code; DCh/field mismatch; unexpected activation; power/SEL/session anomaly; failed restoration.

identified_defects: Source and V2 encode the watt field MS-byte first despite DCMI inheriting IPMI least-significant-byte-first numeric order.
V2 claims action/timing behavior assessment without the Activate command or a limit-exceedance stimulus.
The high-level merged command omits action, correction time and sampling period.
Source misspells `ipmitool` as `dcmitool` for Get and clears the SEL evidence needed for action verification.
reason_for_change: Correct a byte-order defect that can apply the wrong persistent power limit and separate parameter storage/read-back from active enforcement. V3 retains all V2 approval/recovery gates but refuses to infer behavior that the source never activates or stimulates.

new_technical_evidence.title: Data Center Manageability Interface Specification
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Platforms implementing standard DCMI Set/Get/Activate Power Limit
new_technical_evidence.supports: Set Power Limit defines action, watts, correction time and sampling period, is for a static persistent upper limit, and should be followed by explicit Activate to ensure effect. DCMI follows IPMI byte order unless otherwise stated; IPMI numeric fields are least-significant-byte first. Get distinguishes active versus no active limit.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Exact safe ranges, platform-specific OEM codes, desired active state and whether enforcement belongs to this row remain owner/platform-specific.

removed_ambiguities: Corrects multi-byte raw encoding to little-endian by default.
Separates stored configuration read-back from activated enforcement and exception behavior.
Defines all fields rather than a watt-only high-level substitution.
resolved_blockers: Normative DCMI command and byte-order rules resolve the source's encoding question; execution is feasible after exact values and approval.
remaining_blockers: No write may run until safe exact fields, desired activation scope, platform ranges, maintenance approval, fallback and restore are supplied.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 prevents an incorrectly byte-swapped persistent power policy and removes an unsupported claim that Set/Get alone validates power-limit enforcement, while preserving V2's strong high-risk controls.

agent_understanding_result.notes: The endian correction and configuration-versus-enforcement boundary are queued for isolated validation.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The source writes all DCMI action/limit/timing fields and then reads them back but provides no Activate command.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 preserves field completeness and safety but repeats MS-first encoding and expands to behavior assessment without activation/stimulus.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow baseline/capability work; one little-endian Set/Get only after exact approval, with activation/enforcement excluded unless separately specified.
